This fixture is evaluated against a chosen metric—such as calibration delta or entropy—to assess its validity. The falsification step enforces a kill rule that prevents further development if the metric fails to meet criteria. Only after this local validation does the system consider AWS mapping, ensuring scalability only when local proof holds. Finally, publication occurs only if the artifact is both source-safe and caveated. Each step introduces a dualistic structure: local vs. global, synthetic vs. real, and validated vs. speculative. Failure modes arise when metrics fail to detect contradictions or when AWS mapping proceeds without sufficient local support.
